554: 
555: ### Discussion
556: 
557: There was a significant escalation in measles transmission in 2024 compared to previous years, highlighted by the 
558: epidemiological data presented above. A total of 35 212 measles cases were reported, resulting in an overall 
559: notification rate of 77.4 cases per 1 000 000 population — a significant increase compared to the 2023 rate of 5.3 
560: per 1 000 000 population. Romania continued to report the highest notification rate, with 1 610.7 cases per 
561: 1 000 000 population, substantially higher than its 2023 rate (92.2 cases per 1 000 000).
562: 
563: The first half of 2024 showed a particularly sharp increase in measles activity, reaching levels higher than any level 
564: recorded over the past two decades, before it declined again toward the end of the year. In response to this rapid 
565: rise in cases, ECDC issued a dedicated Threat Assessment Brief emphasising the ongoing public health risk, 
566: highlighting concerns around sub-optimal vaccination coverage, the high potential for cross-border transmission, 
567: and the anticipated seasonal peak which further compounded the risk [2].
568: 
569: Similar to previous years, measles continued to affect individuals across all age groups in 2024. Infants under one 
570: year of age were the most severely impacted, showing the highest incidence at 1 175.4 cases per 1 000 000 
571: population. This population group remains particularly vulnerable since infants under one year are typically too 
572: young for direct vaccination and thus rely heavily on population immunity for protection. In 2024, 87% of all cases 
573: with known vaccination status were unvaccinated. Among children aged one to four years, who would typically 
574: receive their first dose of measles vaccine in national vaccination schedules, the rate remained high at 688.7 per 
575: 1 000 000 population, with 90% of these children unvaccinated, underlying the fact that ongoing gaps are present 
576: in this critical age group.
577: 
578: The age distribution of measles cases in 2024 reveals a notable difference between the EU/EEA countries. In 
579: Romania, over one-third of all cases were in children aged 1–4 years, while in several other countries (e.g. Italy, 
580: Spain, France, Poland), the majority of cases occurred in adults aged 30 years and older. This difference may
581: indicate variation in vaccination coverage in the age groups over a longer historical period and the gaps in catch-up 
582: vaccination strategies. Romania’s sharp drop in MCV1 and MCV2 coverage over recent years, especially among 
583: young children, likely facilitated early-age transmission [11]. Conversely, in countries with higher current childhood 
584: coverage but missed vaccinations in the past, older cohorts are now more exposed and at risk of infection [12].
585: 
586: Hospitalisation rates for measles cases remained consistently high in 2024, with 79% of reported cases required
587: hospitalisation. This aligns closely with the 2023 hospitalisation rate of 80% but significantly exceeds earlier figures 
588: from preceding years (33% in 2022 and 55% in 2019). Additionally, most hospitalised individuals—approximately 
589: 85% — were unvaccinated. In 2024, complications from measles were frequently reported, predominantly 
590: affecting unvaccinated individuals. Among hospitalised patients, complications such as pneumonia, otitis media, 
591: and encephalitis continued to be prevalent. Importantly, 2024 recorded 23 measles-related deaths (of which 22 
592: were reported from Romania), a marked increase compared to the three fatalities reported in 2023. Notably, 14 
593: deaths were reported in children below the age of five years.
594: 
595: While the majority of measles cases reported in 2024 originated from local transmission within EU/EEA countries, 
596: among the cases with known importation status, 18% were imported and 7 % were imported-related, and 
597: together counting for 764 cases, which is significantly higher compared to 2023 (6.4%). Most imported infections 
598: were acquired from other European countries, either within the EU/EEA (26%) or non-EU/EEA regions (39%), 
599: followed by Asia (22%) and Africa (4%). Importations from Austria, Germany, Spain, France, Italy, and Romania 
600: collectively accounted for 65% of these cases. This notable increase in imported measles highlights the need and 
601: value of international collaboration, including timely information exchange to prevent further cross-border 
602: transmission and outbreaks within the EU/EEA region. In addition, checking and updating vaccination against 
603: measles should be a routine practice during travel medicine consultations and general health checks prior to 
604: travelling, including those travelling within the EU/EEA [13]. Strengthening exchange of information on crossborder cases via established EU and international channels is important to avoid re-establishment of measles in 
605: receiving countries.
606: 
607: All EU/EEA countries have adopted national, publicly funded childhood vaccination programmes targeting measles, 
608: mumps, and rubella (MMR). Among these, eleven countries — Bulgaria, Croatia, Czechia, France, Germany (under 
609: the Measles Protection Act), Hungary, Italy, Latvia, Poland, Slovakia, and Slovenia—have implemented mandatory 
610: MMR vaccination policies, primarily enforced through school-based mechanisms. France (2018), Germany (2019), 
611: and Italy (2017) recently introduced mandatory vaccination, with preliminary findings indicating increased 
612: vaccination coverage among targeted groups; however, additional analyses are necessary to evaluate the longterm impact and effectiveness of these interventions [14]. Typically, the first MMR dose is scheduled between 12–
613: 18 months of age, with earlier administration (9–11 months) recommended in Austria, Germany, Liechtenstein, 
614: and Slovenia. The timing of the second dose varies considerably across countries, ranging from early in the second 
615: year of life in Austria and Germany to preschool or primary school ages elsewhere. Additionally, catch-up 
616: recommendations vary widely, with Spain, for example, extending vaccination opportunities up to 64 years of age [15].
617: 
618: ---
619: 
620: Modelling studies suggest that in countries with substantial immunity gaps, supplementary immunisation strategies 
621: targeting individuals not covered by existing programmes may be required to achieve interruption of measles 
622: transmission [16].
623: 
624: The latest WHO estimates on national immunisation coverage for 2023 show a slight overall decrease in 
625: vaccination coverage within the EU/EEA compared to previous years; however, the estimates remained relatively 
626: consistent over the last five years. In 2023, the overall weighted vaccination coverage in the EU/EEA was 93.9% 
627: for the first dose (MCV1) and 88.8% for the second dose (MCV2). Six countries reported decreased coverage for 
628: the first measles vaccine dose, with Romania experiencing the most significant reduction (from 83% in 2022 to 
629: 78% in 2023). Similarly, nine countries reported decreased coverage for the second dose. While fifteen EU/EEA 
630: countries (50%) reached the ≥95% threshold for the first vaccine dose, only four countries (14%)—Hungary, 
631: Malta, Portugal, and Slovakia—achieved this threshold for the second dose. This represents a decline compared to 
632: the seven countries (Bulgaria, Hungary, Latvia, Malta, Norway, Portugal, and Slovakia) meeting the ≥95% 
633: benchmark for MCV2 in 2019, highlighting persistent challenges in attaining optimal vaccination coverage required 
634: for measles elimination. It is also to be noted that in two countries there was a positive upward trend of 3% or 
635: above (range up to 7%) when comparing the estimates from 2020 to 2023 for the first dose, and an upward trend 
636: in four countries for the second dose. A downward trend of 3% or more was observed in eight countries, both for 
637: the first and the second dose.
638: 
639: The European Regional Verification Commission for Measles and Rubella Elimination (RVC), which was established 
640: in 2011 [13] monitors the progress of the countries of the WHO European Region in relation to measles and rubella 
641: elimination. During the 12th RCV meeting, held in 2023, with reference to the data of 2022, it was concluded that 
642: 20 EU/EEA Member States provided evidence to demonstrate the elimination of endemic measles, whereas five 
643: countries were considered endemic, three countries were considered to have re-established measles transmission 
644: and for one country, the status is still pending [16].
645: 
646: ### Public health implications
647: 
648: ECDC continues to closely monitor measles activity in the EU/EEA, providing monthly epidemiological updates and 
649: assessments to support Member States' public health actions. ECDC continues to recommend the following actions 
650: for a public health response: closing immunity gaps through achieving and maintaining ≥95% vaccination coverage 
651: with two doses of measles-containing vaccine, enhancing surveillance quality, ensuring rapid detection, diagnosis, 
652: and outbreak control, and raising clinical awareness among healthcare providers. The deployment of upgraded 
653: digitalised immunisation information systems to identify and reach the unvaccinated is also critical and should form
654: an integral part of national efforts to improve the performance and management.
655: 
656: ### Conclusion
657: 
658: In 2024, the EU/EEA region recorded the highest number of measles cases observed in the past two decades, 
659: significantly exceeding pre-pandemic levels. This sharp increase underscores persistent immunity gaps and 
660: vulnerabilities within the population, exacerbated by suboptimal measles vaccination coverage. Although the 
661: impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on immunisation programmes varied by country — with some experiencing 
662: declines and others maintaining or slightly improving coverage — most EU/EEA countries have yet to achieve or 
663: sustain the ≥95% vaccination coverage target with two doses of measles-containing vaccine. Enhanced 
664: epidemiological surveillance, prompt outbreak investigation, and control measures remain critical for interrupting 
665: transmission and achieving regional elimination targets. Urgent action to address existing immunity gaps through 
666: targeted catch-up vaccination campaigns, particularly among populations disproportionately impacted by pandemic 
667: disruptions are essential. Strengthened public health communication and accelerated efforts to enhance vaccine 
668: acceptance remain crucial for restoring high immunisation coverage and preventing future measles outbreaks in 
669: the EU/EEA.

41: ## England measles epidemiology 2025
42: 
43: This report describes measles epidemiology in England from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025.
44: 
45: ## Summary
46: 
47: From 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025 there were 958 laboratory-confirmed measles cases reported in England. Measles case numbers started to increase in April 2025 with outbreaks particularly affecting London and the North West. However, after mid-July activity stabilised, and remained relatively stable till the end of the year. Data for [2023 and 2024](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-epidemiology-2023) and [historical data](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-confirmed-cases/confirmed-cases-of-measles-in-england-and-wales-by-region-and-age-2012-to-2014) are available. Total number of cases by week of onset from 2024 can be found on the the [UKHSA data dashboard](https://ukhsa-dashboard.data.gov.uk/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles).
48: 
49: The number of laboratory-confirmed measles cases by month of symptom onset in 2025 were:
50: 
51: - January: 88
52: - February: 68
53: - March: 69
54: - April: 110
55: - May: 129
56: - June: 127
57: - July: 118
58: - August: 50
59: - September: 29
60: - October: 42
61: - November: 70
62: - December: 58
63: 
64: The majority (654 out of 958, 68%) of these cases were in children aged 10 years and under, and 25% (243 out of 958) were in young people and adults aged 15 years and over (Table 1). 52% (494 out of 958) of these cases have been in London, 14% (132 out of 958) in the North West, and 8% (76 out of 958) in the East of England. However, all regions have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025. 101 upper tier local authorities (UTLAs) have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025, with the highest numbers reported in Hackney (133 out of 958, 14%), Birmingham (52 out of 958, 5%) and Bristol (47 out of 958, 5%) (Table 2a).
65: 
66: The vaccination status of all confirmed cases is published quarterly in the related [health protection reports](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-mumps-and-rubella-lab-confirmed-cases-in-england-2025).
67: 
68: In 2025, one acute measles-related death occurred in a child who was known to have other medical conditions. Information on historical measles-related deaths is available on the [notifications and deaths webpage](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-deaths-by-age-group-from-1980-to-2013-ons-data/measles-notifications-and-deaths-in-england-and-wales-1940-to-2013).

41: ## England measles epidemiology 2025
42: 
43: This report describes measles epidemiology in England from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025.
44: 
45: ## Summary
46: 
47: From 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025 there were 958 laboratory-confirmed measles cases reported in England. Measles case numbers started to increase in April 2025 with outbreaks particularly affecting London and the North West. However, after mid-July activity stabilised, and remained relatively stable till the end of the year. Data for [2023 and 2024](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-epidemiology-2023) and [historical data](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-confirmed-cases/confirmed-cases-of-measles-in-england-and-wales-by-region-and-age-2012-to-2014) are available. Total number of cases by week of onset from 2024 can be found on the the [UKHSA data dashboard](https://ukhsa-dashboard.data.gov.uk/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles).
48: 
49: The number of laboratory-confirmed measles cases by month of symptom onset in 2025 were:
50: 
51: - January: 88
52: - February: 68
53: - March: 69
54: - April: 110
55: - May: 129
56: - June: 127
57: - July: 118
58: - August: 50
59: - September: 29
60: - October: 42
61: - November: 70
62: - December: 58
63: 
64: The majority (654 out of 958, 68%) of these cases were in children aged 10 years and under, and 25% (243 out of 958) were in young people and adults aged 15 years and over (Table 1). 52% (494 out of 958) of these cases have been in London, 14% (132 out of 958) in the North West, and 8% (76 out of 958) in the East of England. However, all regions have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025. 101 upper tier local authorities (UTLAs) have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025, with the highest numbers reported in Hackney (133 out of 958, 14%), Birmingham (52 out of 958, 5%) and Bristol (47 out of 958, 5%) (Table 2a).
65: 
66: The vaccination status of all confirmed cases is published quarterly in the related [health protection reports](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-mumps-and-rubella-lab-confirmed-cases-in-england-2025).
67: 
68: In 2025, one acute measles-related death occurred in a child who was known to have other medical conditions. Information on historical measles-related deaths is available on the [notifications and deaths webpage](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-deaths-by-age-group-from-1980-to-2013-ons-data/measles-notifications-and-deaths-in-england-and-wales-1940-to-2013).

41: ## England measles epidemiology 2025
42: 
43: This report describes measles epidemiology in England from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025.
44: 
45: ## Summary
46: 
47: From 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025 there were 958 laboratory-confirmed measles cases reported in England. Measles case numbers started to increase in April 2025 with outbreaks particularly affecting London and the North West. However, after mid-July activity stabilised, and remained relatively stable till the end of the year. Data for [2023 and 2024](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-epidemiology-2023) and [historical data](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-confirmed-cases/confirmed-cases-of-measles-in-england-and-wales-by-region-and-age-2012-to-2014) are available. Total number of cases by week of onset from 2024 can be found on the the [UKHSA data dashboard](https://ukhsa-dashboard.data.gov.uk/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles).
48: 
49: The number of laboratory-confirmed measles cases by month of symptom onset in 2025 were:
50: 
51: - January: 88
52: - February: 68
53: - March: 69
54: - April: 110
55: - May: 129
56: - June: 127
57: - July: 118
58: - August: 50
59: - September: 29
60: - October: 42
61: - November: 70
62: - December: 58
63: 
64: The majority (654 out of 958, 68%) of these cases were in children aged 10 years and under, and 25% (243 out of 958) were in young people and adults aged 15 years and over (Table 1). 52% (494 out of 958) of these cases have been in London, 14% (132 out of 958) in the North West, and 8% (76 out of 958) in the East of England. However, all regions have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025. 101 upper tier local authorities (UTLAs) have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025, with the highest numbers reported in Hackney (133 out of 958, 14%), Birmingham (52 out of 958, 5%) and Bristol (47 out of 958, 5%) (Table 2a).
65: 
66: The vaccination status of all confirmed cases is published quarterly in the related [health protection reports](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-mumps-and-rubella-lab-confirmed-cases-in-england-2025).
67: 
68: In 2025, one acute measles-related death occurred in a child who was known to have other medical conditions. Information on historical measles-related deaths is available on the [notifications and deaths webpage](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-deaths-by-age-group-from-1980-to-2013-ons-data/measles-notifications-and-deaths-in-england-and-wales-1940-to-2013).

41: ## England measles epidemiology 2025
42: 
43: This report describes measles epidemiology in England from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025.
44: 
45: ## Summary
46: 
47: From 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025 there were 958 laboratory-confirmed measles cases reported in England. Measles case numbers started to increase in April 2025 with outbreaks particularly affecting London and the North West. However, after mid-July activity stabilised, and remained relatively stable till the end of the year. Data for [2023 and 2024](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-epidemiology-2023) and [historical data](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-confirmed-cases/confirmed-cases-of-measles-in-england-and-wales-by-region-and-age-2012-to-2014) are available. Total number of cases by week of onset from 2024 can be found on the the [UKHSA data dashboard](https://ukhsa-dashboard.data.gov.uk/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles).
48: 
49: The number of laboratory-confirmed measles cases by month of symptom onset in 2025 were:
50: 
51: - January: 88
52: - February: 68
53: - March: 69
54: - April: 110
55: - May: 129
56: - June: 127
57: - July: 118
58: - August: 50
59: - September: 29
60: - October: 42
61: - November: 70
62: - December: 58
63: 
64: The majority (654 out of 958, 68%) of these cases were in children aged 10 years and under, and 25% (243 out of 958) were in young people and adults aged 15 years and over (Table 1). 52% (494 out of 958) of these cases have been in London, 14% (132 out of 958) in the North West, and 8% (76 out of 958) in the East of England. However, all regions have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025. 101 upper tier local authorities (UTLAs) have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025, with the highest numbers reported in Hackney (133 out of 958, 14%), Birmingham (52 out of 958, 5%) and Bristol (47 out of 958, 5%) (Table 2a).
65: 
66: The vaccination status of all confirmed cases is published quarterly in the related [health protection reports](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-mumps-and-rubella-lab-confirmed-cases-in-england-2025).
67: 
68: In 2025, one acute measles-related death occurred in a child who was known to have other medical conditions. Information on historical measles-related deaths is available on the [notifications and deaths webpage](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-deaths-by-age-group-from-1980-to-2013-ons-data/measles-notifications-and-deaths-in-england-and-wales-1940-to-2013).

41: ## England measles epidemiology 2025
42: 
43: This report describes measles epidemiology in England from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025.
44: 
45: ## Summary
46: 
47: From 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025 there were 958 laboratory-confirmed measles cases reported in England. Measles case numbers started to increase in April 2025 with outbreaks particularly affecting London and the North West. However, after mid-July activity stabilised, and remained relatively stable till the end of the year. Data for [2023 and 2024](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-epidemiology-2023) and [historical data](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-confirmed-cases/confirmed-cases-of-measles-in-england-and-wales-by-region-and-age-2012-to-2014) are available. Total number of cases by week of onset from 2024 can be found on the the [UKHSA data dashboard](https://ukhsa-dashboard.data.gov.uk/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles).
48: 
49: The number of laboratory-confirmed measles cases by month of symptom onset in 2025 were:
50: 
51: - January: 88
52: - February: 68
53: - March: 69
54: - April: 110
55: - May: 129
56: - June: 127
57: - July: 118
58: - August: 50
59: - September: 29
60: - October: 42
61: - November: 70
62: - December: 58
63: 
64: The majority (654 out of 958, 68%) of these cases were in children aged 10 years and under, and 25% (243 out of 958) were in young people and adults aged 15 years and over (Table 1). 52% (494 out of 958) of these cases have been in London, 14% (132 out of 958) in the North West, and 8% (76 out of 958) in the East of England. However, all regions have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025. 101 upper tier local authorities (UTLAs) have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025, with the highest numbers reported in Hackney (133 out of 958, 14%), Birmingham (52 out of 958, 5%) and Bristol (47 out of 958, 5%) (Table 2a).
65: 
66: The vaccination status of all confirmed cases is published quarterly in the related [health protection reports](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-mumps-and-rubella-lab-confirmed-cases-in-england-2025).
67: 
68: In 2025, one acute measles-related death occurred in a child who was known to have other medical conditions. Information on historical measles-related deaths is available on the [notifications and deaths webpage](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-deaths-by-age-group-from-1980-to-2013-ons-data/measles-notifications-and-deaths-in-england-and-wales-1940-to-2013).

41: ## England measles epidemiology 2025
42: 
43: This report describes measles epidemiology in England from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025.
44: 
45: ## Summary
46: 
47: From 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025 there were 958 laboratory-confirmed measles cases reported in England. Measles case numbers started to increase in April 2025 with outbreaks particularly affecting London and the North West. However, after mid-July activity stabilised, and remained relatively stable till the end of the year. Data for [2023 and 2024](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-epidemiology-2023) and [historical data](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-confirmed-cases/confirmed-cases-of-measles-in-england-and-wales-by-region-and-age-2012-to-2014) are available. Total number of cases by week of onset from 2024 can be found on the the [UKHSA data dashboard](https://ukhsa-dashboard.data.gov.uk/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles).
48: 
49: The number of laboratory-confirmed measles cases by month of symptom onset in 2025 were:
50: 
51: - January: 88
52: - February: 68
53: - March: 69
54: - April: 110
55: - May: 129
56: - June: 127
57: - July: 118
58: - August: 50
59: - September: 29
60: - October: 42
61: - November: 70
62: - December: 58
63: 
64: The majority (654 out of 958, 68%) of these cases were in children aged 10 years and under, and 25% (243 out of 958) were in young people and adults aged 15 years and over (Table 1). 52% (494 out of 958) of these cases have been in London, 14% (132 out of 958) in the North West, and 8% (76 out of 958) in the East of England. However, all regions have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025. 101 upper tier local authorities (UTLAs) have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025, with the highest numbers reported in Hackney (133 out of 958, 14%), Birmingham (52 out of 958, 5%) and Bristol (47 out of 958, 5%) (Table 2a).
65: 
66: The vaccination status of all confirmed cases is published quarterly in the related [health protection reports](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-mumps-and-rubella-lab-confirmed-cases-in-england-2025).
67: 
68: In 2025, one acute measles-related death occurred in a child who was known to have other medical conditions. Information on historical measles-related deaths is available on the [notifications and deaths webpage](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-deaths-by-age-group-from-1980-to-2013-ons-data/measles-notifications-and-deaths-in-england-and-wales-1940-to-2013).

41: ## England measles epidemiology 2025
42: 
43: This report describes measles epidemiology in England from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025.
44: 
45: ## Summary
46: 
47: From 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025 there were 958 laboratory-confirmed measles cases reported in England. Measles case numbers started to increase in April 2025 with outbreaks particularly affecting London and the North West. However, after mid-July activity stabilised, and remained relatively stable till the end of the year. Data for [2023 and 2024](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-epidemiology-2023) and [historical data](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-confirmed-cases/confirmed-cases-of-measles-in-england-and-wales-by-region-and-age-2012-to-2014) are available. Total number of cases by week of onset from 2024 can be found on the the [UKHSA data dashboard](https://ukhsa-dashboard.data.gov.uk/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles).
48: 
49: The number of laboratory-confirmed measles cases by month of symptom onset in 2025 were:
50: 
51: - January: 88
52: - February: 68
53: - March: 69
54: - April: 110
55: - May: 129
56: - June: 127
57: - July: 118
58: - August: 50
59: - September: 29
60: - October: 42
61: - November: 70
62: - December: 58
63: 
64: The majority (654 out of 958, 68%) of these cases were in children aged 10 years and under, and 25% (243 out of 958) were in young people and adults aged 15 years and over (Table 1). 52% (494 out of 958) of these cases have been in London, 14% (132 out of 958) in the North West, and 8% (76 out of 958) in the East of England. However, all regions have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025. 101 upper tier local authorities (UTLAs) have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025, with the highest numbers reported in Hackney (133 out of 958, 14%), Birmingham (52 out of 958, 5%) and Bristol (47 out of 958, 5%) (Table 2a).
65: 
66: The vaccination status of all confirmed cases is published quarterly in the related [health protection reports](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-mumps-and-rubella-lab-confirmed-cases-in-england-2025).
67: 
68: In 2025, one acute measles-related death occurred in a child who was known to have other medical conditions. Information on historical measles-related deaths is available on the [notifications and deaths webpage](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-deaths-by-age-group-from-1980-to-2013-ons-data/measles-notifications-and-deaths-in-england-and-wales-1940-to-2013).

41: ## England measles epidemiology 2025
42: 
43: This report describes measles epidemiology in England from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025.
44: 
45: ## Summary
46: 
47: From 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025 there were 958 laboratory-confirmed measles cases reported in England. Measles case numbers started to increase in April 2025 with outbreaks particularly affecting London and the North West. However, after mid-July activity stabilised, and remained relatively stable till the end of the year. Data for [2023 and 2024](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-epidemiology-2023) and [historical data](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-confirmed-cases/confirmed-cases-of-measles-in-england-and-wales-by-region-and-age-2012-to-2014) are available. Total number of cases by week of onset from 2024 can be found on the the [UKHSA data dashboard](https://ukhsa-dashboard.data.gov.uk/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles).
48: 
49: The number of laboratory-confirmed measles cases by month of symptom onset in 2025 were:
50: 
51: - January: 88
52: - February: 68
53: - March: 69
54: - April: 110
55: - May: 129
56: - June: 127
57: - July: 118
58: - August: 50
59: - September: 29
60: - October: 42
61: - November: 70
62: - December: 58
63: 
64: The majority (654 out of 958, 68%) of these cases were in children aged 10 years and under, and 25% (243 out of 958) were in young people and adults aged 15 years and over (Table 1). 52% (494 out of 958) of these cases have been in London, 14% (132 out of 958) in the North West, and 8% (76 out of 958) in the East of England. However, all regions have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025. 101 upper tier local authorities (UTLAs) have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025, with the highest numbers reported in Hackney (133 out of 958, 14%), Birmingham (52 out of 958, 5%) and Bristol (47 out of 958, 5%) (Table 2a).
65: 
66: The vaccination status of all confirmed cases is published quarterly in the related [health protection reports](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-mumps-and-rubella-lab-confirmed-cases-in-england-2025).
67: 
68: In 2025, one acute measles-related death occurred in a child who was known to have other medical conditions. Information on historical measles-related deaths is available on the [notifications and deaths webpage](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-deaths-by-age-group-from-1980-to-2013-ons-data/measles-notifications-and-deaths-in-england-and-wales-1940-to-2013).

41: ## England measles epidemiology 2025
42: 
43: This report describes measles epidemiology in England from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025.
44: 
45: ## Summary
46: 
47: From 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025 there were 958 laboratory-confirmed measles cases reported in England. Measles case numbers started to increase in April 2025 with outbreaks particularly affecting London and the North West. However, after mid-July activity stabilised, and remained relatively stable till the end of the year. Data for [2023 and 2024](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-epidemiology-2023) and [historical data](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-confirmed-cases/confirmed-cases-of-measles-in-england-and-wales-by-region-and-age-2012-to-2014) are available. Total number of cases by week of onset from 2024 can be found on the the [UKHSA data dashboard](https://ukhsa-dashboard.data.gov.uk/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles).
48: 
49: The number of laboratory-confirmed measles cases by month of symptom onset in 2025 were:
50: 
51: - January: 88
52: - February: 68
53: - March: 69
54: - April: 110
55: - May: 129
56: - June: 127
57: - July: 118
58: - August: 50
59: - September: 29
60: - October: 42
61: - November: 70
62: - December: 58
63: 
64: The majority (654 out of 958, 68%) of these cases were in children aged 10 years and under, and 25% (243 out of 958) were in young people and adults aged 15 years and over (Table 1). 52% (494 out of 958) of these cases have been in London, 14% (132 out of 958) in the North West, and 8% (76 out of 958) in the East of England. However, all regions have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025. 101 upper tier local authorities (UTLAs) have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025, with the highest numbers reported in Hackney (133 out of 958, 14%), Birmingham (52 out of 958, 5%) and Bristol (47 out of 958, 5%) (Table 2a).
65: 
66: The vaccination status of all confirmed cases is published quarterly in the related [health protection reports](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-mumps-and-rubella-lab-confirmed-cases-in-england-2025).
67: 
68: In 2025, one acute measles-related death occurred in a child who was known to have other medical conditions. Information on historical measles-related deaths is available on the [notifications and deaths webpage](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-deaths-by-age-group-from-1980-to-2013-ons-data/measles-notifications-and-deaths-in-england-and-wales-1940-to-2013).

41: ## England measles epidemiology 2025
42: 
43: This report describes measles epidemiology in England from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025.
44: 
45: ## Summary
46: 
47: From 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025 there were 958 laboratory-confirmed measles cases reported in England. Measles case numbers started to increase in April 2025 with outbreaks particularly affecting London and the North West. However, after mid-July activity stabilised, and remained relatively stable till the end of the year. Data for [2023 and 2024](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-epidemiology-2023) and [historical data](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-confirmed-cases/confirmed-cases-of-measles-in-england-and-wales-by-region-and-age-2012-to-2014) are available. Total number of cases by week of onset from 2024 can be found on the the [UKHSA data dashboard](https://ukhsa-dashboard.data.gov.uk/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles).
48: 
49: The number of laboratory-confirmed measles cases by month of symptom onset in 2025 were:
50: 
51: - January: 88
52: - February: 68
53: - March: 69
54: - April: 110
55: - May: 129
56: - June: 127
57: - July: 118
58: - August: 50
59: - September: 29
60: - October: 42
61: - November: 70
62: - December: 58
63: 
64: The majority (654 out of 958, 68%) of these cases were in children aged 10 years and under, and 25% (243 out of 958) were in young people and adults aged 15 years and over (Table 1). 52% (494 out of 958) of these cases have been in London, 14% (132 out of 958) in the North West, and 8% (76 out of 958) in the East of England. However, all regions have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025. 101 upper tier local authorities (UTLAs) have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2025, with the highest numbers reported in Hackney (133 out of 958, 14%), Birmingham (52 out of 958, 5%) and Bristol (47 out of 958, 5%) (Table 2a).
65: 
66: The vaccination status of all confirmed cases is published quarterly in the related [health protection reports](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-mumps-and-rubella-lab-confirmed-cases-in-england-2025).
67: 
68: In 2025, one acute measles-related death occurred in a child who was known to have other medical conditions. Information on historical measles-related deaths is available on the [notifications and deaths webpage](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-deaths-by-age-group-from-1980-to-2013-ons-data/measles-notifications-and-deaths-in-england-and-wales-1940-to-2013).

43: ## England measles epidemiology 2026
44: 
45: This report describes measles epidemiology in England from 1 January 2026.
46: 
47: ## Situational update
48: 
49: In 2024 there were 2,911 laboratory-confirmed measles cases in England, the highest number of cases recorded annually, since 2012. In 2025, there were a total of 958 laboratory-confirmed measles cases. Data for [2023 to 2026](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-epidemiology-2023) and [historical data](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-confirmed-cases/confirmed-cases-of-measles-in-england-and-wales-by-region-and-age-2012-to-2014) are available.
50: 
51: Between 1 January 2026 and 12 October 2026, there have been 1,030 laboratory-confirmed measles cases reported in England. An additional 27 cases were reported since the last publication on 17 September 2026 (Figures 1 and 2). In 2026, measles activity started to increase in February, peaked in May and has declined and stabilised since then.
52: 
53: ## Summary
54: 
55: The number of laboratory-confirmed measles cases by month of symptom onset in 2026 to date are:
56: 
57: - January: 105
58: - February: 142
59: - March: 144
60: - April: 156
61: - May: 215
62: - June: 154
63: - July: 52
64: - August: 33
65: - September: 26
66: - October: 3 (to date)
67: 
68: The [UKHSA data dashboard](https://ukhsa-dashboard.data.gov.uk/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles) provides tabular data on the total number of cases by week of onset in 2026.
69: 
70: The majority (629 out of 1,030, 61%) of these cases were in children aged 10 years and under, and 33% (339 out of 1,030) were in young people and adults aged 15 years and over (Table 1). 50% (520 out of 1,030) of these cases have been in London, 16% (162 out of 1,030) in the West Midlands, and 11% (111 out of 1,030) in the North West. However, all regions have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2026. A total of 98 upper tier local authorities (UTLAs) have reported at least one confirmed case with symptom onset since January 2026, with the highest numbers reported in Enfield (111 out of 1,030, 11%), Birmingham (82 out of 1,030, 8%) and Hertfordshire (64 out of 1,030, 6%) (Table 2a).
71: 
72: The vaccination status of all confirmed cases is published quarterly in the related [health protection reports](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-mumps-and-rubella-lab-confirmed-cases-in-england-2026).
73:

### Epidemiology

Measles is a highly contagious acute viral disease which affects individuals of all ages and remains one of the leading causes of death among young children globally. The mode of transmission is airborne or via droplets from the nose, mouth, or throat of infected persons.

Initial symptoms, which usually appear 10-14 days (range 7-23 days) after infection, include high fever, usually accompanied by a runny nose, bloodshot eyes, cough and tiny white spots inside the mouth. The rash usually appears 10-14 days after exposure and spreads from the head to the trunk to the lower extremities. A person is infectious from four days before up to four days after the appearance of the rash. There is no specific antiviral treatment for measles, and most people recover within 2-3 weeks.

Measles is usually a mild or moderately severe disease. However, measles can lead to complications such as pneumonia, diarrhoea, secondary ear infection, inflammation of the brain (encephalitis), blindness, and death. Postinfectious encephalitis can occur in about one in every 1000 reported cases. About two or three deaths may occur for every 1000 reported cases.

Vaccination with measles containing vaccine is safe and effective, providing protection against measles and its complications for all eligible populations. WHO recommends two doses of Measles Containing Vaccine (MCV) to be provided through the routine immunization schedule. WHO further recommends the conduct of Supplementary Immunization Activities (SIAs) or mass immunization campaigns as an effective strategy for delivering vaccination to children who may have been missed by routine services. ### WHO risk assessment

Measles is a highly contagious viral disease that affects susceptible individuals of all ages and remains one of the leading causes of death among young children globally. Measles can cause serious illness in at-risk groups, including children under 5 years of age, those who are malnourished especially those with vitamin A deficiency and people with weakened immune systems. Measles complications include hearing loss, diarrhoea, pneumonia and blindness. Severe complications of measles include encephalitis, brain damage, and death.

The current outbreak in Bangladesh is occurring in the context of suboptimal population immunity. A substantial proportion of cases occurred among children who were either unvaccinated or had received only one dose of measles-containing vaccine. In addition, some children were infected before reaching the age of eligibility for vaccination at 9 months. Most cases (91%) occurred among children aged 1 to 14 years, indicating substantial immunity gaps in this age group.

Before this outbreak, Bangladesh had made substantial progress towards measles elimination. Reported coverage with the first dose of measles-containing vaccine increased considerably between 2000 (89% - WUENIC) and 2016 (118% - WUENIC), while coverage with the second dose also improved between its nationwide introduction in 2012 (22% - WUENIC) and 2024 (121% - WUENIC). During the same period, confirmed measles incidence declined sharply. However, recent declines in MR1 and MR2 coverage due to nationwide stockout of MR vaccine between 2024-2025, combined with routine immunization gaps and the absence of regular nationwide supplementary measles-rubella campaigns since 2020, have increased the number of susceptible children and contributed to the current outbreak.

The risk at the national level is assessed as high due to ongoing transmission across multiple divisions, the large number of susceptible children, documented immunity gaps, and the occurrence of suspected measles-related deaths. The concentration of cases among unvaccinated and under-vaccinated children including infants too young to be vaccinated, raises concern for continued uninterrupted transmission and severe disease outcomes.

Overall, the outbreak suggests a reversal from Bangladesh’s previous progress towards measles elimination and highlights increasing vulnerability to sustained transmission. Continued spread is likely unless urgent measures are implemented to strengthen surveillance, rapidly detect and respond to cases, and close immunity gaps through high-quality vaccination activities.

There are considerable risks of cross-border spread, facilitated by cross-border population movement, with major urban centres such as Dhaka, Chattogram, Sylhet, and Cox’s Bazar being important international travel and transit hubs increasing the likelihood of national and international spread, particularly among unvaccinated or inadequately vaccinated travelers.

Measles is endemic across the South-East Asia region. The risk is assessed as high at regional level.

Bangladesh shares extensive land borders with India and Myanmar, and population mobility across these borders may facilitate continued transmission. In Myanmar there is a considerable number of unvaccinated/zero dose children. With ongoing conflict and humanitarian crisis, surveillance and response capacities are limited. India, despite achieving high vaccination coverage, has reported a rise in case count over the past six months. Cities with high incidence such as Jashore and Chapainawabganj (an identified hotspot) share busy land crossings with India, thereby increasing the risk of introduction across the border. Despite Bangladesh’s progress towards measles elimination the current outbreak highlights the vulnerability of the population and underscores the fragility of immunization gains.

The risk at the global level is assessed as moderate due to high levels of population mobility, combined with ongoing widespread measles transmission and immunity gaps.

WHO recommends maintaining sustained homogeneous coverage of at least 95% with the first and second doses of the MCV vaccine in all municipalities and strengthening integrated epidemiological surveillance of measles and rubella to achieve timely detection of all suspected cases in public, private, and social security healthcare facilities.

Measles is a highly contagious acute viral disease which affects individuals of all ages and remains one of the leading causes of death among young children globally. The mode of transmission is airborne or via droplets from the nose, mouth, or throat of infected persons.

Measles can cause serious illness in at-risk groups, including children under 5 years of age, those who are malnourished especially those with vitamin A deficiency and people with weakened immune systems.
